facts.raw_span: A 26-year-old man presented with a several-year history of persistent round lesions with a scar-like appearance on his face
His condition had previously been diagnosed and treated unsuccessfully
He denied experiencing previous inflammation and had no history of chicken pox, acne or traumatic lesions in those areas
Several round atrophic lesions on his face, symmetric and bilateral, located especially on the malar and preauricular areas, with a diameter of 5 to 10 mm
The skin lesions were not indurated and displayed no epidermal changes
Histopathologic examination: Showed significant epidermal dell and superficial dermal lymphocytic infiltrate associated with dermal fibrosis
Orcein stain demonstrated reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis beneath the epidermal dell
Figure 1: Shows atrophic lesions on the patient's left cheek (A) and with a cicatricial appearance on the preauricular right area (B)
Figure 2: A) Panoramic histological view shows slight depression of the epidermis (hematoxylin-eosin; original magnification, ×2)
Figure 2: B) Orcein staining shows reduction in elastic fibers beside lymphocytic perivascular infiltrate compared with surrounding healthy area (orcein; original magnification, ×10)
located especially on the malar and preauricular areas
with a diameter of 5 to 10 mm
